records.record_title: Minns Government delivers $350,000 boost for Rehab In The Home in southern Lake Macquarie
records.substantive_excerpt: Minns Government delivers $350,000 boost for Rehab In The Home in southern Lake Macquarie | NSW Government menu Open Menu MyServiceNSW Logged in MyServiceNSW Manage account Logout of MyServiceNSW Ministerial media release Minns Government delivers $350,000 boost for Rehab In The Home in southern Lake Macquarie Published: 7 September 2026 Released by: Minister for Health, Minister for Regional Health Listen The Minns Government is investing $350,000 to expand Rehab In The Home services across southern Lake Macquarie, helping more people access rehabilitation and recovery services closer to home. Rehab In The Home enables eligible patients to receive rehabilitation care in their own homes, supporting recovery while reducing the need to travel for appointments. Funded as part of the 2026-27 State Budget, the investment will support allied health professionals from Hunter New England Local Health District to deliver the expanded community-based services to the southern Lake Macquarie region. The services will include community orthopaedic rehabilitation as well as discharge supports for patients returning home from Central Coast hospitals. The expansion builds on the successful rollout of nurse practitioner-led wound care, continence and aged care outreach clinics in early 2025, which have experienced increasing demand. As one of the fastest-growing areas in the region, southern Lake Macquarie continues to see increasing demand for local health services. The expanded outreach and rehabilitation services will make it easier for older people, people living with disability or mobility challenges, and families to access the care they need closer to home. This investment reflects the NSW Government's commitment to ensuring people living in growing communities can access high-quality healthcare services when and where they need them. This year the Minns Government delivered a $10.3 billion boost to health services across NSW as part of the 26-27 Budget, the largest increase to the health budget in the state’s history. As the population gets older and health systems around the world experience significant pressure, this record investment ensures a more sustainable future for NSW healthcare. records.substantive_excerpt: Next Stage of Hume Highway Upgrade at Table Top to start | NSW Government menu Open Menu MyServiceNSW Logged in MyServiceNSW Manage account Logout of MyServiceNSW Ministerial media release Next Stage of Hume Highway Upgrade at Table Top to start Published: 9 September 2026 Released by: Minister for Regional NSW Listen The Minns Labor Government is continuing work to improve one of Australia’s busiest freight and transport corridors, with the next stage of a major upgrade to the Hume Highway at Table Top to begin later this month. Transport for NSW is upgrading a 3.3 kilometre section of the northbound lanes and a 3.15 kilometre section of the southbound lanes, delivering a smoother, safer and more durable road surface while reducing the need for ongoing maintenance. Work includes road reconstruction and resurfacing, drainage improvements, new safety barriers, updated signs and line marking. The first stage of the project, covering the southern 1.65 kilometres of the northbound lanes and upgrades to two crossovers, was completed in June 2026. The next stage will upgrade the remaining 1.65 kilometres of the northbound lanes, with work planned to start on Friday 18 September and take around 12 weeks to complete, weather permitting. Stage three, covering the southbound lanes, will be carried out next financial year. During stage two, the Tynan Road intersection with the Hume Highway will close from Friday 25 September, with changed traffic conditions also in place at the Burma Road intersection. Traffic controls and temporary safety measures will be in place throughout the work to safely manage vehicles through the area and minimise risks while crews are working near the intersections. Motorists will use the same detours and traffic arrangements that were successfully implemented during the first stage of work. At least one lane will remain open in each direction during construction. Motorists should expect lane closures, contraflow arrangements on the southbound lanes and reduced speed limits through the work zone. Most work will be carried out Monday to Friday between 6am and 11pm, and on Saturdays between 7am and 5pm.
